message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: pr

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - symfony-5

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: Code build, lint and tests
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v1

    - name: Cache Composer dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.composer/cache
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-composer-${{ hashFiles('**/composer.lock') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-composer-

    - name: Platform
      run: uname -m

    - name: Build
      run: make env=ci start

    - name: DDD LAYERS
      run: make env=ci layer

    - name: DB Schema validation
      run: make env=ci schema-validate

    - name: Static tools (analyzers)
      run: make env=ci cs-check;make env=ci phpstan;make env=ci layer;make env=ci psalm

    - name: Tests
      run: make env=ci conf="--coverage-clover build/logs/clover.xml" phpunit

    - name: ARTIFACT
      run: make env=ci artifact

    - name: Coveralls
      run: make env=ci coverage",
  "rationale": "The workflow invokes `make env=ci` in every step, so PHP/Composer dependencies are fetched repeatedly across PR runs. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (supported by the literature report and the measured experiment example) shows caching dependency downloads saves CI time while preserving all checks. Adding an actions/cache@v4 step for the Composer cache, keyed on composer.lock, reuses downloaded dependencies across runs and across the repeated `make env=ci` invocations without removing or altering any build, lint, test, schema-validation, static-analysis, or coverage step. No permissions are weakened, no secrets or new network access are added, and all required checks are retained.",
  "evidence_ids": ["P-LIT-GHA-CACHE", "experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2"]
}
